You are adding five new services to Parallax, an AI research agency in /Users/mac/Documents/Hacks/parallax (TypeScript, Node 24 runs .ts directly, no build). It is a hackathon entry (neatHack, judged on agents that finish substantial tasks reliably: planning, tool use, state, recovery, verification). Every answer is checked from two independent angles: **Records** (Crustdata structured databases) and **Field** (open web: Crustdata web search + page reads), an **Arbiter** settles conflicts, a **Verifier** checks claims in plain code, and a **CFO** prices jobs and enforces a hard budget.

Read first, fully: CLAUDE.md, server/src/context.ts (step(), say(), charge/assertBudget, BudgetExceeded, Permanent), server/src/crust.ts (companySearch, companyEnrich, peopleAt, webSearch, webFetch, readPages, directFetch, usablePage, countryNames), server/src/llm.ts (json() with check + repair), server/src/agents/compare.ts (same(), quoteOnPage(), quoteSupports(), people()), server/src/agents/cfo.ts (PRIOR, unitsOf, quote), server/src/catalog.ts, server/src/runner.ts (SERVICES map), server/src/services/company-brief.ts and lead-list.ts (the two existing services: copy their patterns: checkpointed step() per unit of work so resume works, say() narration, quotes verified against page text, plain-code checks, BudgetExceeded handling, partial delivery).

## Build these services (ids exactly as given)

Add a `dept` field to every catalog entry: 'sales' | 'market' | 'trust' (company-brief and lead-list are 'sales').

1. **people-map** (sales) "Who to talk to": input {company, goal} (e.g. "selling HR software"). Lead works out which functions matter for the goal; Records finds current people at the company by those functions/titles (peopleAt with several title groups, rank seniority); Field confirms each person on the open web (search "Name Company", snippet must mention surname + company, flag "former/ex-/left"). Deliver 3-8 people with role, why they matter for the goal, confirmation checks. Unit for pricing: 1 map.
2. **competitor-teardown** (market): input {company, focus} . Resolve the company (like company-brief resolve). Records finds 4-6 competitors (companySearch semantic on the company's description, same country optional, exclude itself); Lead screens them with one model call. For each competitor (step per competitor): Records gives headcount/founded/funding from the search fields/enrich; Field reads its homepage (+ /pricing if it exists, via readPages) and extracts positioning one-liner, target customer, pricing (if stated) each with an exact quote verified by quoteOnPage. Then a Writer step produces "how the client differs / where it's exposed" points citing only verified items (reuse the audit idea from company-brief: cites must exist, no hedging words). Unit: 1 teardown.
3. **market-map** (market): input {space, country?, count}. Like lead-list without people: companies in the space with name, domain, headcount, founded, funding, HQ (Records), each confirmed by Field reading its homepage with a quoted line showing what it does (quoteOnPage). Reuse lead-list's search filters, screening and DNS liveness ideas (factor shared helpers into a module if useful, e.g. server/src/services/shared.ts, without breaking lead-list). Unit: per company delivered, like lead-list (partial delivery on budget).
4. **vendor-check** (trust) "Check before you pay": input {company (name or domain), context} e.g. "supplier asking for a 50% deposit". Produce a verdict green / amber / red with evidence. Signals, each a check {name, ok, severity, note, source}: domain resolves and site loads; Records has a company record and it matches the name/domain; founded year and headcount plausible; a named leader exists in the people database AND on the web; web search for complaints/scam/fraud/lawsuit mentions (Field reads snippets, quotes them; an LLM classifies each snippet as about THIS company or not, quote must be in the snippet); news check. The verdict is computed in plain code from the checks (e.g. any high-severity fail → red; 2+ medium → amber), never by an LLM alone. Unit: 1 check.
5. **person-check** (trust) "Verify a person": input {name, company, title?}. Records: person search by name + current employer domain/name → current title, start date, profile URL; Field: web search for the person + company → snippets confirming/contradicting (former/left), plus the company's own team/about page if found. Verdict: confirmed / mismatch / not found, computed in code. Unit: 1 check.

## Output shape (so the web UI can render every service generically)
Every new service returns an object with:
```
{
  headline: string,                       // one-sentence answer, plain words
  verdict?: 'green' | 'amber' | 'red' | 'confirmed' | 'mismatch' | 'not-found',
  facts?: Resolved[],                     // two-angle fact rows (same type as company-brief) when relevant
  items?: { title: string; subtitle?: string; link?: string; status: 'verified' | 'dropped'; checks: { name: string; ok: boolean; note: string; severity?: 'low'|'medium'|'high' }[]; fields?: Record<string, string>; dropReason?: string }[],
  points?: { text: string; cites: string[] }[],
  stats: Record<string, number>,          // include counts like verified/checked/conflicts
  csv?: string,
  partial?: boolean, priceUsd?: number
}
```
Also add `headline` (and keep everything else) to the existing company-brief and lead-list results, without changing their other fields.

## Wire-up
- server/src/catalog.ts: entries with id, name, dept, blurb, fields (name, label, placeholder, type?) for each new service.
- server/src/runner.ts: add to SERVICES and WORKFLOW_NAMES (workflow name = service id).
- server/src/agents/cfo.ts: PRIOR entry per new service (estimate from the call pattern: Crustdata web search 1 credit/query, page fetch via Crustdata 1 credit/page but readPages tries a free direct fetch first, company enrich 2 credits, company/person search ~0.03-0.25/result; credits are valued at $0.01; models are cheap) and unitsOf for market-map (per company like lead-list).
- server/src/types.ts: add the new ServiceIds.
- server/evals/cases.ts: add one eval case per new service (realistic inputs, e.g. people-map for Paystack selling HR software; competitor-teardown for Linear; market-map "AI agent observability tools", United States, 5; vendor-check for a real company like "Paystack" plus a likely-fake domain; person-check for "Karri Saarinen, Linear, CEO"), and extend scripts/eval.ts so they run and record generic rows (status, cost, secs, stats, verdict). Keep existing cases untouched.

## Rules
- Typecheck must pass: `cd server && npx tsc --noEmit -p .`.
- Test each new service with ONE real job at the end, via a small script (e.g. server/scripts/try.ts <service> '<json input>') that calls createJob + runJob in-process with tag 'dev' and prints the result headline, stats and cost. BEFORE running any live test, wait until /Users/mac/Documents/Hacks/parallax/data/eval-v4.log contains "wrote evals" (an eval is running and Crustdata's web search limit is 10/min; don't compete). Poll with sleep loops in bash. Keep total spend small (each test should cost under ~$0.40). Run the API env with `node --env-file=../.env`. Never print keys.
- Do NOT touch web/ (someone else is rebuilding the UI right now) and do NOT git commit or push (the lead will commit). Do not restart or kill any running processes (an API server on :8787 and an eval process are running).
- Match the existing code style: concise, comments only where they explain why, plain-English say() lines that a client could read in a live timeline.
- Fix bugs you find in the live tests (Crustdata field names: check live responses; the docs index is at https://docs.crustdata.com/llms.txt).

When done, report: files changed, each service's live test result (headline, verdict/stats, cost, trace id from job.traces), anything that failed or that you were unsure about.

# Parallax

An AI agency that checks every answer from two angles. Entry for neatHack (neatlogs.com/hackathon), Oct 10–12 2026.
Build log and submission checklist: `hackathon.md` (keep it updated after each work session, dated entries, evidence links only).

## How it works

- `server/` — Hono API on Node 24, `.ts` run directly (no build). `npm run dev` from `server/` (port 8787, reads `../.env`).
- A **job** = one neatlogs `WORKFLOW` trace (`runner.ts`). Each unit of work is a checkpointed `step()` (`context.ts`): saved to `data/jobs/<id>.json`, skipped on resume, retried with backoff, traced as an `AGENT` span. Crustdata calls are `TOOL` spans (`crust.ts`); model calls go through `wrapOpenAI` (`llm.ts`).
- Agents: Lead (intake/plan), CFO (`agents/cfo.ts`: quote from past cost per unit, hard budget, books), Records (Crustdata database), Field (Crustdata web search + fetch), Arbiter (conflict tiebreak), Verifier (quote-on-page + value checks, plain code in `agents/compare.ts`), Writer.
- Services: `services/company-brief.ts`, `services/lead-list.ts`.
- Spend is charged per call (`charge()`); `assertBudget()` stops a job at its cap → status `paused`, resumable via `/api/jobs/:id/approve`.
- Fault injection for recovery demos: `PARALLAX_CHAOS="crust:0.3,llm-json:0.3"`.

## Rules that matter

- All code must be written during the hackathon (Oct 10–12). Commits are judged for dates.
- Must use neatlogs (tracing), Entire (checkpoints/graph/brain) and cfo.ai (business plan). Demo ≤3 min covering all three.
- Push with plain `git push` (the pre-push hook uploads Entire checkpoints). Commit messages: no AI co-author or "generated with" lines.
- Never commit `.env` or keys. Never put keys, personal data or private traces in `hackathon.md`.

## Next up

1. Run real jobs once `.env` has LITELLM_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY, CRUSTDATA_API_KEY; fix Crustdata field mappings against live responses.
2. Eval harness (`server/scripts/eval.ts`): fixed set of briefs, score verified-facts / lead precision / cost / latency, tagged runs → before/after numbers from neatlogs traces.
3. Web app (`web/`): hire form → CFO quote → live job view (two angles side by side, conflicts, checks, money) → books page.
4. Deploy (Railway), demo video, cfo.ai plan from measured unit economics.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `400` | Invalid request: unsupported field, wrong operator, malformed filters, or an invalid or mismatched `cursor`. |
| `401` | Invalid or missing API key. |
| `403` | Permission denied, preview mode not enabled for your account, or insufficient credits. |
| `500` | Internal server error. Retry with exponential backoff. |

### No results

When no people match the filters, the API returns `200` with an empty `profiles` array:

```json theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
{
    "profiles": [],
    "next_cursor": null,
    "total_count": 0,
    "total_count_relation": null,
    "remarks": []
}
```

To fix an empty result, do one of these:

* Send the request again with `"explain": true` to learn which condition removed every result. See [Remarks](#remarks).
* Use wider filters.
* Check the field values with [Autocomplete](/person-docs/autocomplete/introduction).

<Note>
  To match many values of a field, put all of them in one `in` condition, not
  in many separate conditions. The API runs one `in` condition as one
  efficient query. An `in` list of up to about 5,000 to 10,000 values returns
  in a few seconds. Larger lists get slower, and the API rejects very large
  lists of about 50,000 values or more. For a larger set, split the values
  into chunks of about 5,000 to 10,000. Send one request for each chunk, and
  merge the results. The request body has a hard limit of 10 MB. A larger
  body returns `413 request_too_large`. With typical payloads, you reach the
  query-size limit first.
</Note>

## Five new services: built and each tested live

All five services are built, wired up and passed one real job each, after fixes from earlier live runs. Typecheck passes (`cd server && npx tsc --noEmit -p .`). I did not commit, push, touch `web/`, or restart or kill any process. I waited for "wrote evals" in `eval-v4.log` before the first live call.

**Restart needed:** the API on :8787 is still running the old code. It won't serve the new services until someone restarts it.

### Live test results (tag `dev`, final run of each)
| Service | Job | Result | Cost | Trace |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| person-check (Karri Saarinen, Linear, CEO) | job_mv3ktk0667bd | **confirmed**: database, web snippet and linear.app/about all agree; title "CEO, Cofounder" matches | $0.046 | c555673b5d5003e3af12246e6a531f30 |
| people-map (Paystack, selling HR software) | job_mv3kyk9oexct | "7 people to talk to at Paystack… start with Kristin Clarke (Head of People). 7 of 7 confirmed on the open web." Approach plan passed the audit on the first draft | $0.114 | b069edc0336443e6f64afcea93a2f6ad |
| competitor-teardown (Linear) | job_mv3kx0vx24d8 | GitHub, Asana, monday.com, ClickUp; 11 of 12 quotes verified; 6 points | $0.162 | 7cc877219fa807cca73a8a888d2f496b |
| market-map (AI agent observability tools, US, 5) | job_mv3kstjp9asv | 5 of 5 mapped (Braintrust, Latitude, ClawMetry, Trodo, Netra), 2 dropped, 3 with funding | $0.107 | 3ef9709828be0ca75140f88efc08990b |
| vendor-check (paystack.com) | job_mv3kihq1u7j0 | **green**, 12 of 14 checks; minor fails: CBN fine, 3 complaints | $0.082 over two runs | 726390b6a211cf531c992d99479bb7f2 and 23c2cd3bccc33d06886a3ace2e8c40d4 |
| vendor-check (globalsteel-procurement-ng.com) | job_mv3kfw07g28w | **red**: domain doesn't exist, no company record, no leader | $0.012 | 4c490efe0c1014718692338dc1af1c96 |
| company-brief (Linear), regression check after the refactor | job_mv3l0680ae7a | 7 of 7 facts verified; new headline works | $0.150 | cb20b3c94ec0fa3e5dda25b069bf22f5 |

The Paystack vendor-check first paused at a $0.05 budget, because the CFO priced it from the two cheap fake-domain runs. I resumed it with `scripts/try.ts --resume`; it kept its 5 finished steps and delivered. That run is a real budget-stop-then-resume example. Total spend across about 13 test jobs was roughly $1.5.

### Bugs found and fixed
- **Already in your services:** the "Work order" line never showed up in any job timeline. `say()` was called outside a `step()`, so it had no agent context and was silently dropped. All six services now send it as the Lead.
- **Left-the-company flag:** "ex-/former" fired on other people in the same snippet (e.g. a comment's "ex-Paystack"), and on "former Google engineer …, CEO of Linear". It now has to appear in the same piece of text as the person's surname. This also changes lead-list.
- **Short names like "Linear":** the database search returned only lookalikes. It now asks the web for the official site, then looks that domain up exactly; when a domain is given it tries an exact lookup, then enrich.
- **Competitor search:** a search on the description alone returned one-person AI startups. The Lead now names up to 6 rivals with domains, Records confirms them with one exact lookup, and that is merged with the semantic search. There's also a headcount floor and the company's own name is stripped from the query.
- **Pricing quotes:** these are stitched from table cells and never matched word for word. Quotes joined with "..." now pass only if every piece is on the page, and a price also passes if every price in it is printed on the page. A `$0` price used to fail the money check; that's fixed.
- **Web search sometimes comes back empty** for a query that has results, and charges nothing. vendor-check retries once on an empty result, and a failed search shows up as a check instead of counting as "no complaints".
- **CFO pricing:** with fewer than 3 past jobs, the starting estimate is now the minimum per-unit cost, so a couple of cheap early runs can't shrink the budget.

### Files changed
- **New:** `server/src/services/` `shared.ts`, `people-map.ts`, `competitor-teardown.ts`, `market-map.ts`, `vendor-check.ts`, `person-check.ts`, plus `server/scripts/try.ts`.
- **Edited:**
  - `src/types.ts`: new service ids, `Dept`, `Verdict`, `Check`, `Item`, `Deliverable`.
  - `src/catalog.ts`: `dept` on every entry, plus the five new entries.
  - `src/runner.ts`: added to SERVICES and WORKFLOW_NAMES.
  - `src/agents/cfo.ts`: PRIOR entries, `unitsOf` for market-map, `unitName`, the floor above.
  - `src/crust.ts`: `fields`/`mode` on company search, `FUNDING_FIELDS`, `companiesByDomain`, `personSearch`, function and seniority options on `peopleAt`.
  - `src/api.ts`: `/books` unit names per service, and `live.items` for the new services.
  - `src/services/company-brief.ts` and `lead-list.ts`: use the shared helpers, gained `headline`; no other result fields changed.
  - `evals/cases.ts`: `SERVICE_CASES`, six cases with expected verdicts.
  - `scripts/eval.ts`: `--only` accepts `services` or a list; one generic row per case (status, cost, secs, verdict, verdictOk, headline, stats).
  - `CLAUDE.md`: the services line.

### Not done or unsure
- lead-list was not re-run live after its refactor; it typechecks and the logic is unchanged.
- The new eval section was not run (about $0.6).
- Empty web results could also cause false "not confirmed on the web" in company-brief, lead-list, people-map and person-check. Moving the retry-once into `crust.webSearch` itself would cover them; I didn't, because it changes existing services' latency.
- Competitor-teardown points can still be a bit opinionated even without hedge words. I tightened the prompt but haven't re-run it since.
- My dev-tagged jobs now count in CFO history, which doesn't filter by tag.
- I didn't update `hackathon.md`.
